{{Quote|The Chiss do not simply accept alien concepts without careful consideration. We certainly do not submit to domination. By anyone.|[[Mitth'raw'nuruodo/Legends|Thrawn]]|<ref name="Outbound Flight (novel)">[[Outbound Flight (novel)|''Outbound Flight'']]</ref>}}
The '''Chiss Ascendancy''', sometimes termed '''Chiss Space''' or the '''Chiss Empire''' by outsiders, was a portion of [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]] just inside the [[Unknown Regions/Legends|Unknown Regions]] that was ruled by the [[Chiss/Legends|Chiss]].

==History==
{{Quote|&hellip;our experience with Grand Admiral Thrawn taught us that insularity could be a weakness as well as a strength. It's not enough to be strong; a truly successful culture needs to be flexible as well. And in order to be flexible, we must look beyond what we consider familiar; we must come to know our neighbors as well as we know ourselves.|[[Commander/Legends|Commander]] [[Hess'irolia'nuruodo|Irolia]]|<ref name="Refugee">''[[The New Jedi Order: Force Heretic II: Refugee]]''</ref>}}
[[File:Chiss_Ascendancy-SWTOR.svg|thumb|right|250px|An alternative insignia of the Chiss Ascendancy during the Order of Zildrog campaign.]]
The Chiss were a very [[Speciesism|xenophobic]] people, believing themselves to be superior to all other beings; this attitude led to an isolationist society, and largely by choice. The Chiss rarely engaged in trade with anyone from outside their borders. Despite their isolation and prejudices, Chiss goods, like [[Charric/Legends|charrics]], could be found in Republic markets by [[3951 BBY]].<ref name="KOTORII">''[[Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic II: The Sith Lords]]''</ref>

When the [[Sith Empire (Post–Great Hyperspace War)|Sith Empire]] returned in [[3681 BBY]] to fight the Republic once more, during the [[Great Galactic War]] and the [[Cold War (Galactic Republic–Sith Empire)|Cold War]], the Chiss Ascendancy was the only true ally of the Empire, unlike all the other species and worlds that the Empire subjugated; indeed, some Chiss were known to serve as [[Imperial Agent]]s.<ref name="Daniel Erikson">[[w:c:swtor:User_blog:Ausir/Daniel_Erickson_answers_your_questions|Interview with Daniel Erickson at SWTOR Wiki]]</ref> When the [[Eternal Empire]] [[Eternal Empire conquest|conquered the galaxy]] in [[3636 BBY]], the Ascendancy ceded its two richest industrial worlds to Emperor [[Arcann]] as tribute, in exchange for the Ascendancy's continued autonomy. When the Eternal Empire fell to the [[Eternal Alliance|Alliance]] [[3630 BBY|six years later]], the Ascendancy quickly reclaimed the worlds with the aid of the Sith Empire.<ref>{{TORcite|type=codex|The Chiss Ascendancy and the Eternal Empire}}</ref>

At some point, prior to [[1000 BBY/Legends|1000 BBY]], the [[Brotherhood of Darkness/Legends|Brotherhood of Darkness]] raided the Unknown Regions to bolster their own forces. As part of this operation, a regiment of Chiss were relocated to [[Thule/Legends|Thule]]. Nearly a thousand years later, before the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]], [[Count/Legends|Count]] [[Dooku/Legends|Dooku]] recruited the [[The Force/Legends|Force]]-sensitive Chiss General [[Sev'rance Tann/Legends|Sev'rance Tann]] and her lover, [[Vandalor]], to the armed forces of the [[Confederacy of Independent Systems/Legends|Confederacy of Independent Systems]].<ref name="TEA">''[[The Essential Atlas]]''</ref> During the Clone Wars, the Ascendancy held diplomatic meetings with the Republic, with [[Aristocra/Legends|Aristocra]] [[Sev'eere'nuruodo]] meeting with the Republic's representative, the Chiss [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] [[Padawan/Legends|Padawan]] [[Nuru Kungurama|Kung'urama'nuruodo]]. The Chiss' position was to stay neutral in the conflict.<ref name="TSM2">''[[The Clone Wars: Secret Missions 2: Curse of the Black Hole Pirates]]''</ref>

During the later stages of the [[Yuuzhan Vong]] War, the Chiss joined the [[Galactic Federation of Free Alliances]] in the fight against the invaders, and apparently maintained closer relations with the Galactic Alliance following the peace treaty.

One of the Ascendancy's major conflicts was the [[Swarm War]]. A race of intelligent insectoid beings, the Killiks, were disrupting Chiss space. This would eventually lead to all-out war against the Killiks, when [[Darth Caedus|Jacen Solo]] and his friends executed a sneak attack on [[Supply Depot Thrago]] to prevent Jacen's catastrophic vision from coming true. The Galactic Alliance would eventually be caught up in the mix once they realized it was the [[Gorog|Dark Nest's]] influence on the colony that was provoking the war. The war was ended after the capture of the Colony's leader, [[Raynar Thul]], and the destruction of the Dark Nest with the death of [[Lomi Plo]] after the death of [[Welk]].<ref name="The Swarm War" />

During the [[Sith–Imperial War]], the Chiss were dragged into the conflict on the [[Fel Empire]]'s side when [[Fehlaaur'aitel'loro]], the Chiss diplomat to the Empire, was made a [[Moff/Legends|Moff]], the head of the [[Imperial Diplomatic Corps/Legends|Imperial Diplomatic Corps]] and placed on the [[Council of Moffs/Legends|Moff Council]].<ref name="LECG">''[[Legacy Era Campaign Guide]]''</ref>

[[Darth Krayt's Galactic Empire]] allowed the Ascendancy to retain much of its autonomy. However, it maintained some control over Ascendancy by making heads of Chiss houses high-ranking officials within the new Empire. It also gave the Ascendancy control over large tracts of the [[Unknown Regions/Legends|Unknown Regions]].<ref name="LECG" /> In [[138 ABY]], as the [[Second Imperial Civil War]] escalated following the [[Final Protocol|poisoning]] of [[Dac/Legends|Dac]] and the return of [[Darth Krayt]], the Ascendancy remained neutral, though, like the [[Hapes Consortium/Legends|Hapes Consortium]], it did not even reply to Imperial requests for open liaisons.

==Organization==
===Government===
{{Quote|We Chiss are accustomed to formulating our own policies.|[[Aristocra/Legends|Aristocra]] [[Chaf'orm'bintrano|Formbi]]|<ref name="The Swarm War">''[[Dark Nest III: The Swarm War]]''</ref>}}
[[File:Csilla_NEGAS.jpg|thumb|left|170px|Csilla, capital of the Ascendancy]]
The Chiss were governed by an oligarchy of extended [[Ruling Families/Legends|Ruling Families]] from [[House Palace]], located in the city of [[Csaplar/Legends|Csaplar]]. Each clan with the families was headed by leaders known as [[Aristocra/Legends|Aristocra]] who wore particular colors to indicate their clan and family loyalties. Standard and day-to-day decisions were made by a democratically-elected parliamentary body from each of the 28 colonies. Issues were siphoned up through the parliament to a cabinet of appointed [[Governor/Legends|governors]], and then to the ruling families, where a decision made by the parliament and/or cabinet could be approved for action. Each of the extended ruling families was responsible for a set of government affairs to manage: [[Sabosen family|House Sabosen]] was responsible for social issues such as justice, health, and education; [[Inrokini family|House Inrokini]] was responsible for industry and science; [[Csapla family|House Csapla]] was responsible for colonial affairs, agriculture, and redistribution of resources; and [[Nuruodo family|House Nuruodo]] was responsible for military and foreign affairs. The Csapla's redistribution of resources amongst the Chiss colonies and Csilla was particularly important, given the collectivist-socialist economic system of the Chiss, and led to their relative position at the head of the families, with the others acting in an advisory role. House Nuruodo would be ranked as second, considering the importance of warfare on Chiss society.

Each family was equally represented in the Chiss government, although they went to great lengths to ensure that family identity was eliminated wherever possible. The leaders of the Chiss did not use names, but instead wore colorful robes to distinguish themselves. This helped ensure that decisions were reached in a fair and equitable method. Although the four extended ruling families were not known to face power struggles, five lesser clans often vied for greater authority and power, such as [[Chaf family/Legends|House Chaf]], which was considered the fifth ruling family.

The vast financial holdings of the Chiss kept their supply lines running and also provided them access to a number of independent shipyards which they used to keep their vessels on constant patrol. It was through such methods that the Chiss maintained a poacher base at the [[Rodian Hunting Grounds|Etyyy]] hunting grounds on [[Kashyyyk/Legends|Kashyyyk]].

===Military===
[[File:Chiss_UAA.jpg|thumb|right|150px|A member of the Chiss species.]]
{{Quote|He has his orders, and when a Chiss accepts orders he carries them out, period.|[[Chak Fel]] on [[Prard'ras'kleoni|Drask]]|<ref name="Survivor's Quest">''[[Survivor's Quest]]''</ref>}}
The military of the Chiss Ascendancy consisted of a well trained and well armed force which protected a number of advanced and orderly worlds within its sphere of influence. Chiss belief in rigid discipline was further seen within their armed forces and they made use of superior technology when required in order to hold enemy forces at bay. Ultimately, the Chiss saw themselves as a bastion of order in a sea of chaos in their home space in the Unknown Regions.<ref name="TUR">''[[The Unknown Regions]]''</ref>

While their history was marked by nearly continual warfare and conquest of other worlds, the Chiss were generally not violent. They preferred to extend themselves only from a defensive posture, although they were exposed to threats in the Unknown Regions and [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim]], such as the [[Ssi-ruu]]k and the threat of the [[Vagaari/Legends|Vagaari]] (who fought [[Vagaari Wars|three wars]] with the Chiss), the [[Yuuzhan Vong War]] in which is the reason Thrawn went to Palpatine in the first place, to help defeat the threat of the Yuuzhan Vong in the Unknown regions, and the later [[Killik/Legends|Killik]] [[Swarm War|incursion]]. There were two military organizations: the [[Chiss Expansionary Defense Force]] and the [[Phalanx (Chiss)|Colonial Phalanx]]es, which were both led by the Nuruodo family. The Chiss Expansionary Defense Fleet patrolled the Chiss borders and space, although segments were known to combat forces beyond the realm of the Chiss in times of dire need. This fleet was considered to be a tool of [[Wikipedia:Foreign affairs|foreign affairs]] rather than a military asset. Each of the 28 colonies was protected by a phalanx, which was commanded by a [[Syndic/Legends|Syndic]], or House leader, and responsible for handling any threats that slipped past the fleet. In times of crisis, Chiss Expansionary Defense Fleet segments drew upon the nearby phalanxes to strengthen themselves and tighten border patrols. The formation of the [[Chiss Army]] and Navy was tributary, with each Chiss colony world sending a complete phalanx to Csilla for command by the Nuruodo family.

Around [[978 BBY]],<ref name="Chiss law date">The [[defensive-only doctrine]] is established to be 1,000 years old during the events of ''[[Survivor's Quest]]'', which takes place in [[22 ABY/Legends|22 ABY]] per ''[[The Essential Reader's Companion]]''. Therefore, it must have been established around [[978 BBY]].</ref> the Ascendancy passed the [[defensive-only doctrine]], prohibiting preemptive warfare.<ref name="Survivor's Quest" />

==Astrography==
In total, the Ascendancy consisted of Csilla and twenty-eight inhabited colonies, although the Ascendancy contained several hundred thousand star systems within or near its borders. Information on all planets and star systems visited by the Chiss was kept in the [[Expeditionary Library]] on Csilla.<ref name="Refugee" />

===Notable locations===
*[[Avidich/Legends|Avidich]] &mdash; A vertiginous world of high peaks and dizzying drops, Avidich was used by the Chiss to cultivate edible lichens.
*[[Brask Oto Command Station|Brask Oto]] &mdash; [[Chiss Expansionary Defense Force|CEDF]] space station serving as the barbican for the Redoubt.
*[[Celwis/Legends|Celwis]] &mdash; This colony along the Vagaari Corridor, once raided with regularity by alien aggressors, showcased a decisive demonstration of Chiss military strength shortly after the formation of the CEDF.
*[[Cioral/Legends|Cioral]] &mdash; Home of [[Csapla family|House Csapla]], this planet was heavily urbanized, yet is responsible for overseeing the Ascendancy's half-dozen agricultural colonies.
*[[Copero/Legends|Copero]] &mdash; Home of [[Mitth family/Legends|House Mitth]], this world was the location of the Chiss Ascendancy's largest shipyard.
*[[Cormit/Legends|Cormit]] &mdash; Location of one of the two major [[Chiss Expansionary Defense Force|CEDF]] bases.
*[[Crustai]] &mdash; Colony world where Chaf'orm'bintrano later rendezvoused with ''Jade Sabre'' en route for ''[[Outbound Flight]]''.
*[[Csaus/Legends|Csaus]] &mdash; Home of [[Inrokini family|House Inrokini]], Csaus was the Ascendancy's hub of science and communications.
*[[Csilla/Legends|Csilla]] &mdash; Ice-covered [[Homeworld/Legends|homeworld]] and political capital of the Chiss. Site of the city of [[Csaplar/Legends|Csaplar]] and the [[Expeditionary Library]].
*[[Jamiron/Legends|Jamiron]] &mdash; This world appeared barren from space, but hid hydroponic Ag facilities inside its porous crust.
*[[Kinoss/Legends|Kinoss]] &mdash; Location of one of the two major [[Chiss Expansionary Defense Force|CEDF]] bases.
*[[Klasse Ephemora system/Legends|Klasse Ephemora]] &mdash; This system contained the gas giant Mobus, around which the living planet Zonama Sekot orbited until late in the Yuuzhan Vong War.
*[[Mobus/Legends|Mobus]] &mdash; Gas giant in the [[Klasse Ephemora system/Legends|Klasse Ephemora system]]. [[Zonama Sekot/Legends|Zonama Sekot]] sought refuge in a lunar orbit around Mobus after its flight from its home system in [[29 BBY/Legends|29 BBY]], and from [[30 ABY/Legends|30 ABY]], Zonama Sekot was resettled by the Yuuzhan Vong remnant.
*[[Naporar/Legends|Naporar]] &mdash; Home of the [[Nuruodo family]] and location of the CEDF headquarters.
*[[Ool/Legends|Ool]] &mdash; A forested planet spotted with vast circular plots of farmland.
*[[Oyokal/Legends|Oyokal]] &mdash; An aquaculture colony of fish-stocked pools and wave-riding algal beds, Oyokal was home to a quadrupedal native species.
*[[Pesfavri/Legends|Pesfavri]] &mdash; Location of a [[Chiss Defense Fleet]] base near the redoubt.
*[[The Redoubt/Legends|The Redoubt]] &mdash; Dense star cluster developed as an interstellar fortress by the Chiss. Site of [[Brask Oto Command Station|Brask Oto]] and the unnamed planet on which ''[[Outbound Flight]]'' came down.
*[[Rentor/Legends|Rentor]] &mdash; The Chiss settlements on this world were constructed atop icebergs that slowly cruised the ocean currents.
*[[Rhigar/Legends|Rhigar]] &mdash; Site of a Chiss military academy in the [[Rata Nebula/Legends|Rata Nebula]].
*[[Sarvchi/Legends|Sarvchi]] &mdash; Home of the [[Chaf family/Legends|Chaf family]].
*[[Shihon/Legends|Shihon]] &mdash; All animals on Shihon were boneless, with bulbous gasbags filling the sky and city-sized jellies choking the oceans.
*[[Sposia/Legends|Sposia]] &mdash; Home of [[Sabosen family|House Sabosen]], Sposia held the Ascendancy's top academies and med-centers.
*[[Tenupe]] &mdash; Situated on the Sparkle Run, Tenupe was a jungle world captured by the Chiss Ascendancy from the Killiks in the final battle of the Swarm War.
*[[Thearterra/Legends|Thearterra]] &mdash; An obscure body in the S-K system, this world was perpetually racked by volcanoes, hailstorms, and ground-quakes.
*[[Thrago]] &mdash; Site of a CEDF supply depot anchored around a small moon, destroyed by rogue [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] in [[36 ABY]].
*[[Yashuvhu/Legends|Yashuvhu]] &mdash; Remote hinterland planet with a [[Force-sensitive/Legends|Force-sensitive]] [[Human/Legends|Human]] population; home world of the [[duuvhal]], and of Force-talent [[Valara Saar]].
*[[Catlia]], [[Massoss/Legends|Massoss]], [[Sharb/Legends|Sharb]], [[Noris/Legends|Noris]], [[Schesa/Legends|Schesa]], and [[Ornfra/Legends|Ornfra]] &mdash; These outlying colonies, all homes to former Ruling Families, were largely wiped out prior to the Swarm War. The families on Catlia and Massoss became Joiners, while the others fell on the losing side of a [[Chiss civil conflict|civil conflict]].
